Latest Update: Do Monsters Lurk Around Us in Plain Sight? Gentle Monster’s Director Worries They Do

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A newspaper clipping about a ring of pedophiles captivated the attention of Austrian filmmaker Marie Kreutzer one morning six years ago.
  • According to recent reports, “It was shocking because most of the guys in that ring of criminals were normal family dads,” Kreutzer tells Bazaar on a recent call.
  • In a recent development, kreutzer decided to channel this shock, the all-consuming fear that we cannot trust those we love the most, into her latest film, Gentle Monster.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A newspaper clipping about a ring of pedophiles captivated the attention of Austrian filmmaker Marie Kreutzer one morning six years ago. The article detailed the buildup and the arrest in explicit detail, but one description felt more haunting than the rest.

According to recent reports, “It was shocking because most of the guys in that ring of criminals were normal family dads,” Kreutzer tells Bazaar on a recent call. “It made me so much more aware of how close these perpetrators are, more than we want to think, and that I must almost certainly also know one.… When I read that article, and it described how the police officers were standing at the doorsteps of these guys, my first thought was, ‘How would that be for me if it were my husband?’ ”.

In a recent development, kreutzer decided to channel this shock, the all-consuming fear that we cannot trust those we love the most, into her latest film, Gentle Monster. Releasing on Netflix on November 18, the film tells the story of Lucy Weiss (Léa Seydoux), an experimental pianist who leaves her life behind to raise her young son with her doe-eyed husband, Philip (Laurence Rupp). The trio exists happily in the German countryside, complete with all the comforts of a cozy domestic life. Lucy and Philip love each other and their son, enjoying a sex-filled marriage that appears to have only the regular bumps. This illusion is disrupted when police knock on the door, arresting Philip for his alleged participation in a child pornography ring. Kruetzer designed the couple introduction to feel as if the rug were pulled out from under the viewer.

In a recent development, “It was obviously very notable to have all these scenes where they interact before everything happens and where we see that they have a very natural, loving relationship,” she says. “For me, [Rupp] has nothing secretive or mysterious about him. He’s very there. And that’s what I wanted for the role, because I thought it would be good to see him and never really be open to believing that that guy would really do something like that.” She remembered telling Rupp, “It’s not like you’re playing a petty criminal. You’re playing a liar.” Kruetzer wanted him to “make us want to come back to you.”.

In this way, Rupp embodies an uncanny confidence throughout the entire movie. He, of course, carries a sense of guilt, yet an audience can’t easily parse out the weight of his internal feelings. Kruetzer also refrains from giving too much direction about his innocence or guilt. Even when he is released from prison the first time, his nonchalance diffuses any skepticism; you might believe him when he indicates he has nothing to do with it. And when evidence mounts, including actual files, he twists the story again, telling Lucy he did it for the money. Rupp’s sympathetic portrayal is confusing—enough so that you can understand Lucy’s turmoil. Kruetzer remembers telling him to “play it as if you just messed up the taxes,” and later he told her, “I didn’t really play the monster; I played the gentle.”.

Industry observers note that this portrayal adds weight to Seydoux’s indelible performance as Lucy. The entire film orbits her reaction to this horrific revelation. Seydoux’s anger and forgiveness oscillate at a frenetic pace throughout the movie, pulling the viewer into Lucy’s point of view, as well as what Kreutzer first felt when she read the newspaper clipping.

Casting Seydoux, the director says, felt intuitive. The French actress dove headfirst into the script, expressing great interest in the character and the story. “The subject matter is tough, but the fact that it’s through the woman’s perspective—and not through the victim or perpetrator—it’s through her emotions that the story unfolds [is what interested me],” Seydoux says in Bazaar’s profile from last week. One bone-rattling scene in particular, where Lucy faces off with Philip in a light rain and directly confronts him about his arrest, underscores why she’s considered one of the best living French actresses. “As soon as we turned the camera towards her, it was really surprising what came out of her and what poured out of her,” Kreutzer remarked. “I remember that the crew was in shock.”.

Industry observers note that the main storyline provides enough anxiety and suspense, yet Kreutzer wrote a side plot for Gentle Monster to offer perspective. One of the cops who knocks on the Weiss family door, Elsa (Jella Haase), provides a removed point of view on Lucy’s internal dilemma. The character provides a broader understanding of the crime at the center of this story, emphasizing how widespread and hidden this problem is. “For Lucy, her life is falling apart because of this, whereas for Elsa, it’s just one of many cases, and it’s not even a bad one,” Kreutzer says. “It was notable for me to show the magnitude of the problem and to not let the audience lean back and think, ‘Okay, that’s very dramatic, but it has nothing to do with me.’ ”.

Cider-Braised Sausage and Lentils

📅 16 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (429 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation.
  • More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.
  • extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation. Back in my American reality, it still makes an excellent dinner or hearty weekend lunch. Look for mild smoked Austrian or German sausages, which lean on mellow herbs and warm spices (sometimes, if you’re lucky, they’re also stuffed with a nutty cheese)—this style is already cooked to a safe temperature, but the casing’s texture is greatly improved when seared before reheating. If your shop only carries sweet Italian sausage or something like an apple-stuffed chicken sausage, both work in a pinch. What a treat it will be to actually finish off that gallon of apple cider you impulsively bought last week in the lentil-braising liquid.

More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Sources indicate that add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan. Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

Uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been blessed with natural thick hair (thank you endlessly to my parents for passing along these genetics), but life happens and the effects of constantly being stressed, excessive hot tool use, and tight slicked-back ponytails are starting to manifest in a thinning hairline and some density loss. And I, like most people, have been wondering if all the shampoos that promise to help hair grow back are worth a spot in my hair routine.

According to recent reports, the answer to that? It depends. If you’re wondering if these shampoos directly have anything to do with hair growing, then the answer, according to Y. Claire Chang, MD, board-certified dermatologist, is no. As Dr. Chang goes on to explain, hair growth occurs within the hair follicle, which is beneath the surface of the scalp. Since you are rinsing off shampoo, it only stays on your scalp and hair for a few minutes at best, which limits the amount of time that active ingredients have to interact with hair. “This is one of the biggest misconceptions in hair care,” she says. “Most shampoos marketed for hair growth may not actually stimulate hair growth.”.

Sources indicate that but this doesn’t mean these shampoos are completely ineffective. They do help in the grand scheme of your hair growth journey. You just have to think of hair growth shampoos as one piece in a very substantial puzzle for thicker hair. “Growth-promoting shampoos can play a meaningful part of a hair growth or regrowth journey,” claims Kandice Bailey, MD, board-certified dermatologist and Skin of Color Society member. “However, these types of shampoos are a single asset within our arsenal, a single component of a larger plan.”.

According to recent reports, dr. Chang agrees and goes on to explain that what these shampoos actually do is support scalp health, remove excess oil and product buildup, reduce inflammation, and strengthen hair to minimize breakage. “By reducing breakage, hair may retain more length and appear thicker and healthier,” she says.

So if you’re interested in just keeping your scalp as healthy as possible so that hair has the best environment to thrive in, we say to consider these seven shampoos.

Sources indicate that why We Love It: As Fresh York City-based board-certified dermatologist Hadley King, MD, describes it, this is a scalp-focused cleansing system that comes with a shampoo, conditioner, and treatment to help hair look fuller and feel healthier. Inside, you’ll find key ingredients like salicylic acid, which Dr. King claims helps remove excess sebum, dead skin cells and debris on the scalp, as well as peppermint oil and niacinamide to nourish hair. It also has panthenol, biotin, and caffeine to reduce breakage and boost the scalp’s circulation for increased hair growth. Though it may be drying to some (she says to be careful of the sulfates included), there’s nothing like a set to cut out all the guesswork, and this system makes your hair routine super easy.

Why We Love It: “This shampoo can help to strengthen and support hair growth,” states Dr. Garshick. “It’s especially good for those who regularly color, straighten, perm, or heat style their hair.” It contains nourishing ingredients like shea butter, castor oil, and rice protein that will give both your hair and scalp needed moisture and rebuild broken strands. She adds that castor oil has antifungal properties for extra nourishment. It’s also a clarifying shampoo that will give your hair a deep cleanse and get rid of buildup.

According to recent reports, why We Love It: Excessive hot tool use can wreak havoc on our hair. And worst case scenario, lead to thinning. So for the curling iron enthusiast, this is the shampoo for you.

“It helps maintain a clean, nourished scalp surface, which allows emerging hair strands to grow in stronger and [make them] less prone to breakage,” states Morgan Rabach, MD, board-certified dermatologist and co-founder of LM Medical NYC.

It contains peptides and caffeine to stimulate blood flow on the scalp and support the skin barrier, and biotin to strengthen hair. But what really sets it apart is its proprietary keratin alternative called Karmatin, which adds hydration, strength, and shine without heavy silicones weighing hair down. Dr. King adds that it can also improve hair conditioning and improve your hair’s appearance overall.

In a recent development, why We Love It: How does Nutrafol’s shampoo compare to its storied hair-growth pills? Pretty well. “It works by balancing the scalp’s microbiome and gently exfoliating excess oil and product without stripping essential moisture,” notes Dr. Rabach. “A balanced, hydrated scalp prevents follicle irritation and supports stronger, healthier hair.” It’s made with prebiotics, vegan protein, and antioxidant-rich Australian wild berry extract to strengthen the scalp barrier and promote healthy hair growth. It’s also made with biosurfactants, which gives you a thorough cleanse and a rich lather without stripping your hair of its natural oils. The end result is a clean scalp and added volume, which is all we ever ask of our shampoos.

Recent findings suggest that why We Love It: Of all the oils that are touted to help with hair growth, rosemary oil is the most promising; it has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties to help create the ideal environment for hair to thrive in, and small studies even show that it can be as effective as minoxidil. This shampoo is centered around rosemary oil—mixes in plant proteins and ceramides to nourish the scalp and strands and promote healthy hair growth, which Dr. Garshick says it makes it a great option for anyone looking to keep their scalp healthy and strong. Plus it comes with a lovely rosemary scent that’s super refreshing.

Industry observers note that why We Love It: “This shampoo is a great option for those with thinning hair who want a gentle cleanse with added scalp support,” says Marisa Garshick, MD, board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology. It uses a special complex that combines biomimetic peptides and red clover extract to strengthen the scalp’s skin barrier, and pea sprout extract, which is rich in phytonutrients to help increase hair density and help the hair look fuller. It also has a compound called Redensyl to help reduce shedding (thank the beauty gods) and keep hair healthy overall. Plus, it works wonders in giving your hair a boost in volume, which is always welcomed.

Why We Love It: For when hair needs a full reset, we start with this shampoo. Dr. Garshick says that this is great for gently removing buildup from oil, dirt, and pollution, while also hydrating the scalp. It has hyaluronic acid to add that needed moisture and caffeine to boost circulation. But its special H2-Grow complex, which is made of a blend of apple stem cells, is what protects hair from future damage and helps give hair a ticker, fuller appearance.

What ingredients should you look for in hair growth shampoos?

It has been revealed that “I would look for ingredients that support scalp health, reduce inflammation when present, and improve hair strength,” claims Dr. Chang. “I would also prioritize shampoos with gentle cleansing agents and conditioning ingredients to avoid irritating the scalp or damaging the hair shaft.”.

Some ingredients to look out for include:.

Ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione, and selenium sulfide are known for their antifungal properties to control Malassezia yeast overgrowth and inflammation, per Dr. Bailey, and help create a healthy environment for hair to grow. She adds that ingredients like caffeine may help with hair growth by increasing blood circulation to the scalp, which will increase the delivery of micronutrients to your hair follicles.

Dr. Chang adds that ingredients like salicylic acid can help get rid of buildup, while ingredients like niacinamide will support the skin barrier. She also recommends ingredients like panthenol, biotin, and peptides can help strengthen the hair shaft and reduce the risk of breakage.

Are there any downsides to using a hair growth shampoo?

Hair growth shampoos are generally safe, but there are a few things to consider. Dr. Chang says that some formulations may cause scalp irritation, dryness, allergic contact dermatitis, or buildup. Those with sensitive scalps should especially be careful as it might cause more irritation, so she recommends prioritizing gentle, fragrance-free formulations. And if you’re experiencing persistent irritation, burning, or worsening flaking, you should stop using the shampoo and seek medical advice.

Recent findings suggest that but the biggest downside, she claims, is the unrealistic expectations. “Patients may spend a lot of money on products marketed for hair growth when they may potentially benefit more from medical treatment for an underlying form of hair loss,” she says. So remember that shampoos for hair growth may help, but they’re not the sole solution you should turn to.

What actually works for hair growth?

Dr. Chang states that treatments such as topical minoxidil and PRP have much stronger clinical evidence when it comes to actual hair growth. But the most key part is trying to identify the underlying cause of your hair loss to figure out the appropriate treatment. “Because androgenetic alopecia, telogen effluvium, alopecia areata, and nutritional deficiencies all require different approaches,” she says.

When should someone see a doctor for hair loss?

Dr. Chang says that you shouldn’t be waiting several months to see whether your hair growth shampoo is working. Because hair loss can have many different causes (genetics, hormonal changes, postpartum shedding, stress, nutritional deficiencies, thyroid disorders, autoimmune conditions, certain medications, etc.), it’s always best to see a doctor to figure out the cause and come up with the right treatment.

Robert Pattinson, I’m Begging You For a Quirked-Up James Bond

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that our long international nightmare is finally over: two-time Meme of the Year nominee Robert Pattinson has been chosen as Daniel Craig’s James Bond successor, bringing an end to an exhausting series of “reports” and “leaks” about Amazon’s search for a latest 007.
  • In the hands of another (read: more limited) actor, I’d never suggest such a risky swerve.
  • Recent findings suggest that 20 years ago, Casino Royale was a refreshing reset and a crucial corrective to the overflowing ridiculousness of the Piece Brosnan era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our long international nightmare is finally over: two-time Meme of the Year nominee Robert Pattinson has been chosen as Daniel Craig’s James Bond successor, bringing an end to an exhausting series of “reports” and “leaks” about Amazon’s search for a latest 007. Finally we can stop the debates and fan-casting and let Patts and Denis Villeneuve cook until they’re ready to present their new vision. But that would require a level of restraint that the internet doesn’t typically exercise. Immediately after the protracted process of casting Bond concluded, the internet moved on to naming its dream picks for Bond Girls and Bond Villains (sometimes, to brilliant effect.) I can’t say I have a dog in either fight, at least not right now. My Bond WishList is of a different magnitude altogether: can we make James Bond silly again? Just a little, even, 15 percent goofball?

In the hands of another (read: more limited) actor, I’d never suggest such a risky swerve. But the best thing about Pattinson is his range. Sure, if Villeneuve and co. want to render Bond as the stoic and taciturn gentleman he’s generally been this century, Rob has proven he can do that, as every Tenet truther has been gleefully preaching for the last 24 hours. But more often than not, Pattinson is keen to get weird, whether that’s going Full Freak, as he does in Primetime, or approaching certain archetypal parts with a silly, goofy mood (like his conniving suitor in The Odyssey). He can do a “voice” (Mickey 17), he can do scumbag grime (Good Time), he can do hapless screwball (The Drama). Why not make what’ll be his biggest role to date a little cocktail of all his best elements? (Okay, he can leave the Mickey 17 voice behind.).

Recent findings suggest that 20 years ago, Casino Royale was a refreshing reset and a crucial corrective to the overflowing ridiculousness of the Piece Brosnan era. But in the past two decades, the pendulum has swung back—the gritty reboot has become studios' stock-in-trade. I feel the same way about Batman; the actual risky choice would be to make something less like Nolan’s series that, instead, hewed a little closer to, say, Batman Forever, or even the gothic camp of Tim Burton’s two films.

Sources indicate that of course, Robert Pattinson was at the center of a Batman reboot as well, and the result was a movie that felt more like a spiritual cousin to David Fincher’s Se7en; audiences ate it up so much that the hunger for a sequel persists even after endless delays. When it comes to franchises as high-stakes as Batman or Bond, you can’t trust these increasingly sauceless execs to make anything but the basic choice. There’s no reason to expect Jeff Bezos isn’t texting Denis screenshots from Skyfall for reference from his megayacht at this very moment.

But if there’s anybody capable of putting a little English on the handle while still giving the mainstream what it wants, it’s Massive Bob Pattinson. He could easily make his James Bond a little off, or he could go full seductive cad who smiles like Neil Tenet, has a ki with Q, and charms women with some playful banter instead of simply brooding them into submission. I’m not looking for invisible cars and sharks with lasers, or a Lothario like Roger Moore who speaks in puns. All I’m asking is that we give camp a chance. Because ultimately, the most exciting thing Villeneuve and Pattinson can do to set their Bond apart would be to loosen him up a little.

Swift performing at the 2026 CMAs.

Swift presenting at the CMAs in 2016.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.
  • Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a major, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

Upgrade Your Basics: Best Undershirts for Men in 2026

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that just because you don't see a building's foundation doesn't mean it isn't holding everything up.
  • In a recent development, and while they're certainly good for some added warmth in the winter, there's a common misconception that they can make the wearer too hot.
  • In a recent development, an undershirt is an undershirt is an undershirt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that just because you don't see a building's foundation doesn't mean it isn't holding everything up. In much the same way, the best undershirts for men are the humble base layer of countless great outfits. Many GQ staffers, in fact, wear-test theirs daily, and yet they're often overlooked, even though they've long-perfected their role: to be the protective layer between your gross body and your steezy, attention-hungry shirts and polos.

In a recent development, and while they're certainly good for some added warmth in the winter, there's a common misconception that they can make the wearer too hot. In fact, lightweight, moisture-wicking undershirts made from fabrics like modal, or cotton blends can actually transfer the sweat away from your body, speeding up your cooling down. All that's to say: Undershirts are more than just men’s underwear. They’re the cornerstone of a hall-of-fame fit.

In a recent development, an undershirt is an undershirt is an undershirt. If you want the most straightforward version, the kind that you’re picturing in your head is most likely from Calvin Klein. It’s a classic crewneck undershirt that’s made of a lightweight jersey that’s 100% cotton which has a smooth, very slightly brushed hand that feels worn-in in the best way possible. The slim fit won’t cause any weird bunching or bulging and it’s got enough length to stay tucked even when you’re out on the town cutting rugs.

My colleague, GQ senior commerce editor Avidan Grossman, has been wearing CK's genre-defining undershirts since his high school years. (He could do without the logo at the hem, but has made his peace with it, given that you never see it once it's tucked.) Otherwise, he prizes Calvin Klein's riff for its simple, pared-down design and blessed lack of modern-day frills. After all, not every shirt needs to moisture wick or odor block. If you just want an undershirt that gets the job done, don't overthink it.

Sometimes, sleeves are just too much undershirt. That’s where tanks come in. Also known as A-shirts, the humble, sleeveless tank has been rocked by every heartthrob and neighborhood grandpa as far back as anyone can remember. And while the low neck and lack of sleeves means you’ll practically never see them underneath a button-up, the irony is that they look great shown off with an unbuttoned camp shirt or on their own.

It has been revealed that for the money, we think Hanes takes the cake with their multipack of undershirts. The stretchy ribbed jersey is made of 100% cotton and fits snug with a low neck that’s slightly squared off compared to most tanks. They may cost just under twenty bucks for a pack of six, but they look like a million bucks. “I’ve had buyer's remorse over many a menswear garment over the years,” explains GQ editor Jordan Bowman, "but the one thing that has never let me down is the humble tank top from Hanes. They nailed the fit and the material, and the great thing is, you can buy a pack just about anywhere.".

Industry observers note that if every part of your wardrobe has to be fit for a king, down to the most basics of basics, then CDLP is what we’d recommend, my liege. The reality is that most luxury tees don’t offer much more than the regular stuff. It’s diminishing returns after a certain price point, but CDLP is the notable exception. My colleague, our contributing editor Louis Cheslaw, has put his same CDLP cottons through the ringer year after year, and states they still haven't lost their luster.

It’s a pricey undershirt, for sure, but the high-quality fabric has a silky hand and lightweight feel that’s unparalleled. (It really feels like you’re almost wearing nothing.) Thanks to a wider neckline, you’re a lot less likely to see the tee poking out, too. And if you feel like such a nice T-shirt is wasted as underwear, don’t worry—the cut and shorter length means it looks great untucked, and can double as your regular T-shirt too.

Mack Weldon’s silver series of garments is what happens when you get nerdy about chemistry and fashion (in the best possible way). The Ionic+ technology embeds silver charged silver ions which are naturally antimicrobial into the fabric itself. Essentially, that means bacteria and odor is neutralized, which means you can take it easy on the deodorant. Beyond that, the tees are made of super long staple Supima cotton and a smidge of lycra for an extra silky fee, comfortable stretch, and long-lasting wear.

In a recent development, the main bummer is that they’ll cost you more than most tees, so stocking up for the week can get pricey. Still, it’s one of those undershirts that makes you realize you’ve been settling for squalor—plus, you can bundle up and get 10% off to help offset the sticker shock.

Recent findings suggest that not everything at Uniqlo is a great value. But when it comes to upgraded basics at an affordable price, you’d be hard-pressed to find brand that does it better. When you need an airy, breathable undershirt that's truly lightweight, the Japanese mega-retailer’s AIRism tees are legendary. They’re crafted from a smooth and breathable cotton-polyester-spandex blend that dries swiftly, feels cool to the touch, and fights odors—a triple threat that’ll have sweaty days in a headlock. I personally wear these—they're a failsafe way to save my expensive dress shirts from dreaded pit stains, but they’re also perfect for wearing as a gym shirt. And at just $15 per tee, there’s no other undershirt that can do as much for the price.

It has been revealed that GQ contributor Evan Malachosky was always a little skeptical of Skims, but the brand's tees won him over. He found that Skims’s proprietary fabrics are silky on the skin, and are neither too thin (and therefore exposing), nor too thick (and therefore too hot). Pleasingly, the brand has applied just as much care to its undershirt, even though—or perhaps because—it's designed to look invisible under your clothes. (The design team even thought about cleaning up the seam lines, so nothing would show through.) Made from 100% cotton, and available in an incredibly wide range of sizes, our favorite detail is that it's a little bit longer than the brand's standard tees, so that there's no risk of any unsightly seams being visible at the hemline, either.

If the purpose of an undershirt is to fly under the radar, then it stands to reason that a V-neck one—which remains invisible even when you unbutton your shirt collar—might be the most efficient of all the styles here. You'll still want to trust the classic makers here, which is why our favorite comes from Calvin Klein. Like the Calvin Klein crewneck option above, the fabric is smooth, slightly brushed, and 100% cotton. It's also affordable, and available in not just white, black, and gray, but also a multipack comprising all three. Lastly, CK's trademark slimmer fit means no bunching or bulging risk.

Are these “undershirts” far heavier than the usual ones? Yes. But they never lose their shape, and if you live in a bitterly cold climate, you'll want even your undershirt to max out its warming properties.

The luxury car of undershirts, Falke's premium undershirts go on just as smoothly (and last just as long) as the beloved German brand's famous socks.

You heard it here first: Ralph Lauren's Pony has become the coolest label in menswear again.

When James Bond—well, Daniel Craig as James Bond—needs an undershirt, he wears Sunspel's.

Kirkland Signature is somewhat of a fashion industry secret. These are made of soft, long-staple Egyptian cotton, and they're tube knit, meaning you don't have to worry about any uncomfortable side seams.

Made from rayon and polyester, Hanes’ moisture-wicking undershirts are fast-drying, cool to the touch, and silky smooth, all for just $5 a pop.

If you wanna let your clavicles shine uninhibited by any undershirt peek-age, a V-neck is the best way (short of a tank) to do it.

Cut from a premium cotton, this lightweight undershirt is going to feel a little thicker and warmer than others on this list, purely because Reigning Champ's premium cotton fabrics tend to lean towards the beefier end of the spectrum.

Though Mack Weldon’s 18-Hour Rib Tank doesn’t come with the microbe-smashing odor technology as their Silver crew neck undershirt, it does have an even silkier fabric and plenty of stretch.

The first thing I noticed when I met Wythe's founder was not his jeans, or amazing western shirt. It was actually this ribbed tank.

Undershirts are meant to be that intermediate layer between your outermost layers and your body, a protective guard that keeps your star garments fresh and free of sweat. Therefore, it's materials, construction, and fit that are the main components that determine how good an undershirt (and, well, every garment) actually is.

Recent findings suggest that above all else, your undershirt's fabric should be breathable, soft, comfortable, and, ideally, sweat-wicking. We primarily love undershirts and tanks that are made from high-quality 100% cotton, which has many of those characteristics naturally, but we also feel like there’s a time and place for synthetics, which are often used for their ability to wick away moisture and dry easily—especially for those who run particularly hot. And note: Stretchy materials like Spandex are helpful for comfort, but their elasticity will eventually degrade over time.

Undershirts should almost always fit closer to the body than your regular T-shirts. This is because they’ll be layered underneath another shirt or sweater, and can bunch in odd ways if too baggy. They don’t need to be skin-tight, but they should be slim enough to layer comfortably and long enough to tuck into your shirt. In fact, Peter Middleton, founder of Wythe, even told us that they should fit slim to start, since they are cotton and are knit, and will therefore stretch a little over time. If they are loose to start with, they are only going to become looser and saggier, which is really not the point.

It has been revealed that style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Sources indicate that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

To kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

We lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally upcoming to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

Sources indicate that whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the early 2010s set a nearly impossible goal for young women: naturally perky breasts without any apparent scaffolding.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The summer of 2014, I was a college student working at a small-town lingerie store that lined its walls exclusively with neutrals. Every day, I sold women flesh-toned bras—black if they were really feeling kinky—all while filling my own intimates drawer with the same styles. Undressing in front of a guy that same summer, he voiced genuine disbelief over my nude, industrial-strength strapless bra. He wasn’t so much confused over its gravity-defying function as the fact that it was there, at all.

Industry observers note that the early 2010s set a nearly impossible goal for young women: naturally perky breasts without any apparent scaffolding. But that’s all changing. Pop princess Adela’s exposed bras have become as central to her identity as her electric pink hair. Once left to jiggle freely beneath semisheer cotton, Charli XCX’s chest is now more often displayed in intricate lingerie. Several months back, Saint Laurent’s Spring 2027 front row was littered with boudoir-inspired looks while Prada and Fendi literally sent bras-as-tops down the runway. Bras have come out of hiding.

Somewhere between the “free the nipple” movement in 2012 and the impending #MeToo revolution of 2017, boobs became less of a sexualized spectacle and more of a political battleground. Victoria’s Secret canceled its fashion show as basics-driven intimates brands like Cuup and Arq gained traction for destigmatizing natural shapes. Then, breasts bounced back into cultural focus. The shift might be credited to the climate—conservatism generally propels women to take shelter in traditional femininity, or it is thrust upon them—as well as the twin forces of Sydney Sweeney and semaglutide weight loss. Either way, women got thinner while their chests grew larger—reflecting a beauty standard we hadn’t seen in a generation. Implants entered a new era of demand and dialogue, as celebrities like Kylie Jenner and Megan Fox transparently joined the big-breasted brigade.

It has been revealed that but boobs aren’t just bigger—they’re bolder. Gone are the days of basics and bralettes. It’s all about va-va-voom underwire, satin, and lace—even push-ups have returned to the conversation. Still, “there’s a difference between showing your bra and showing off your bra,” discerns Tara Ocello, director of brand marketing at intimates brand Skarlett Blue.

Last month, the recently revived Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show broadcast Jenner strutting down the runway, her 445-cc-moderate-profile silicones outfitted in a record-breaking $50 million bra. Bella Hadid, Candice Swanepoel, and Adriana Lima demonstrated off the iconic mall brand’s finest embroidered balconettes, lacy push-ups, and satin plunge bras. Angels aside, the reintroduction of these runway collections is also indicative of a shift in consumer product demand—a spokesperson for Victoria’s Secret claims there’s “strong interest” in fashion-forward details like lace, satin, logo hardware, and the brand’s statement shine straps. The Very Sexy Push-Up Bra remains the number one of the three mainline bras in its “Very Sexy” category. “Today’s customer wants a bra that performs beautifully and deserves to be seen,” states a Victoria’s Secret spokesperson. “It’s expanded how customers engage with [our bras] as both foundation pieces and intentional styling elements.”.

The luxury London retailer Agent Provocateur has been positioning its designs as statement pieces since it launched in the mid-’90s—the last time exposed bras enjoyed prevalence. Creative director Sarah Shotton noticed the trend bubbling several years back on the Glastonbury grounds and immediately returned to the design studio. “We predicted this and designed [for it] about a year and a half in advance. I am constantly thinking, could it be worn as an outerwear bra?” she says. “I think if customers are going to invest in it, they want it to work harder than just in the bedroom. Lingerie as outerwear is just getting bigger and bigger.”.

It has been revealed that category transcension is, of course, good for business. Victoria’s Secret reported sales up 10 percent in its second quarter, and Agent Provocateur has also seen revenue growth this year. Eager to capitalize on the movement, contemporary brands like Lioness are now engineering built-in underwear to imitate the effect of an exposed bra. This week, Charlize Theron wore a similar style by Tom Ford to the Governors Awards.

I have, undoubtedly, been influenced. This year, I have spent more money at Victoria’s Secret than cumulatively on lingerie in the past decade—acquiring my own Very Sexy Push-Up, and a turquoise polka-dot number. These are bras I’ve never gravitated toward, let alone purchased, because they seemed like impractical additions to my wardrobe. I’ve had to ask myself: Can you wear leopard-print under a white tee? What if the lace breaches my neckline?

Somewhere between Erin Brockovich and Blake Lively’s character in The Town, an exposed bra—particularly a colorful one—became a media shorthand for unsophistication, and more often than not, sexual availability. In simpler terms: tacky. Now, tacky is trending. Along with diamanté-encrusted snapbacks and sky-high peep-toes, straps in dynamic hues are stretched across the décolleté of It girls en masse. Printed cups are peeking out of the necklines. Some fashionistas are forgoing the shirt altogether. “There's a real cultural shift from polished perfection toward something more expressive, unpredictable, and a little undone,” claims Ocello. Or, perhaps a little more human.

This certainly isn’t a trend for everyone. According to Shotton, Agent Provocateur’s biggest sellers are corsets—a style that was once also considered strictly lingerie, but has since sashayed into the light. One wonders if their popularity is a gateway to full bra-baring, especially as GLP drugs become more readily available, and women more comfortable in their bodies. But with a Blue Wave washing in Woke 3.0, how long do boobs—and their bold accessories—have left? In all seriousness, might we look back on this moment with the same disdain we once reflected on early-aughts raunch culture? Only social media will tell. In the meantime, I plan for my collection to keep growing.

Supersized Fashion: The Rise of Giant Bags, Jewelry, and Accessories

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rosalía was recently spotted walking through the Newly introduced York City streets with a Dana Toder bag over three feet long.
  • In case there was any doubt, the point of view was the bag.
  • There’s something undoubtedly beautiful about taking an everyday object and making it obscenely huge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rosalía was recently spotted walking through the Newly introduced York City streets with a Dana Toder bag over three feet long. Paired with her vintage pink satin ballet platform heels from Junko Shimada, the massive, hulking bag from the emerging designer was the kind of shocking jolt of life and newness that typical fashion paparazzi shots lack.

In case there was any doubt, the point of view was the bag. Supersized bags are ubiquitous right now: Chanel, Acne Studios, and Bottega Veneta all showcased their own versions for fall/winter 2026, but Toder’s took the idea to a new level with its extreme size and concept. Consider the bags just one of the many examples of supersizing the everyday. Chandelier earrings and oversize necklaces have never been so substantial at Saint Laurent and Valentino. Elsewhere, labels like Comme des Garçons, Vaquera, and Givenchy amped up their usual voluminous silhouettes even more for spring/summer 2027. Rising designer Beata Rydbacken is also making the biggest hair clips you’ve ever seen in your entire life.

There’s something undoubtedly beautiful about taking an everyday object and making it obscenely huge. It puts a focus on what some may consider the everyday or mundane and makes it sort of beautifully ludicrous. Dana Toder originally designed her “Baggage Bag” for Krähe, a fashion film by Lili Conzen, shot on 16mm, which will be released in spring 2027. Accompanied by exhibitions in London, Paris, Berlin, and Vienna, which will also showcase the bag, the film questions who gets to be seen in fashion and gives older women the leading roles. “When Lili shared the film’s concept with me, it connected really well with how I see clothes and accessories: as things that go through life with us and hold memories and emotions,” Toder tells ELLE. “I see a woman’s relationship with her bag or her garments as something very emotional and complex. The focus on older women felt especially meaningful when thinking about how those relationships develop over a lifetime.”.

For Toder, it’s also a representation of metaphorical and physical baggage. The print featured on the massive bag combines analog photographs from the ’80s to today, taken by the designer, director, and actresses in the film, and plays a role in showcasing the shared experience across different women, ages, and times. The bag itself was also made with the help of her 80-year-old leatherworking mentor, Shmulik.

“I’m interested in everything that becomes emotionally attached to a bag: the things it holds, the places it has been with us, and how the material changes over time. It might hold an object that reminds you of someone, or the bag itself might remind you of a certain period in your life,” she says.

Sources indicate that “We carry all of that around too. I’m always carrying so much stuff, and I love the sight of a woman digging through her bag, with things falling out. I honestly think it’s one of the most beautiful sights. You’re looking for your keys and suddenly going through things that hold so many memories. Some might have been there for two years, or tucked away in your wallet for what feels like forever. I find something very emotional in that everyday moment, coming across parts of your life that you carry without really thinking about them.”.

In a recent development, seeing the familiar through a campy, oversize lens gives one both feelings of nostalgia and whimsy, and that’s perhaps why we’re experiencing so many humungous accessories lately. In the case of Rydbacken, in addition to her giant hair clips, she’s also made supersized wired earbuds, the biggest studded belt to ever exist, and jumbo pins, with many going viral. In fashion’s current game of scale, the bigger the accessory, the more room it leaves for memory, meaning, and a little bit of spectacle.

What Anthropic’s IPO Means for Fashion

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1304 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic, the US artificial intelligence manufacturer behind Claude, will make its debut on New York’s tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange on Thursday under the ticker ANT, in a closely watched IPO that will test Wall Street’s appetite for — and potential of — the AI boom, amid concerns about the cost of developing the technology and intensifying competition.
  • The manufacturer priced its shares at $83, above the projected $70-78 range, raising $81.3 billion and valuing it at approximately $1.5 trillion.
  • In a recent development, “Anthropic’s IPO is an key bellwether for investor sentiment toward AI,” says Lior Prosor, managing partner at venture capital firm Deep33.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the US artificial intelligence manufacturer behind Claude, will make its debut on New York’s tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange on Thursday under the ticker ANT, in a closely watched IPO that will test Wall Street’s appetite for — and potential of — the AI boom, amid concerns about the cost of developing the technology and intensifying competition.

The manufacturer priced its shares at $83, above the projected $70-78 range, raising $81.3 billion and valuing it at approximately $1.5 trillion. This positions it to be the biggest IPO in history, edging out SpaceX’s June debut. Early trading on Thursday will determine investor appetite.

In a recent development, “Anthropic’s IPO is an key bellwether for investor sentiment toward AI,” says Lior Prosor, managing partner at venture capital firm Deep33. “A successful listing would give the tech giant significant capital and greater confidence in its ability to meet its enormous compute commitments. That should also give corporate customers more confidence in Anthropic as a long-term provider,” Prosor adds, forecasting that a successful IPO for Anthropic would signal strong investor appetite for an eventual listing for its biggest rival, OpenAI.

According to recent reports, anthropic’s ambitions extend far beyond the tech sector. In its IPO prospectus, the company states it wants to make Claude available “across every surface where work happens”, targeting a global “knowledge work” market (i.e., jobs that involve processing information, making decisions and producing content, rather than physical work) that it estimates generated more than $40 trillion in economic value in 2025.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, including CEO Dario Amodei, Anthropic has emerged as one of the industry’s leading developers of large language models, competing with OpenAI and Google. Unlike OpenAI, Google and Meta, which have positioned AI, in part, as a consumer tool for shopping and product discovery, Anthropic has focused more heavily on enterprise applications, from coding, research and data analysis, to workplace productivity and content creation. Though recently, it unveiled its first consumer-facing fashion partnership with J.Crew, in the shape of the brand’s “Style Advisor” AI styling tool, co-developed with Claude.

Anthropic’s market debut comes at a turbulent moment for the tech industry, amid a string of major US server outages, the scandal and resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — which is both an investor in Anthropic and a supplier of its AI chips — and mounting concerns about the AI boom. Amodei himself published an article in September calling for an industry-wide slowdown on AI development to ensure security risks and other AI doomsday fears didn’t spiral out of control.

Sources indicate that for fashion, Anthropic’s debut offers another indication of how the AI market is evolving, as brands consider where — and how much — to invest in the technology. Luxury executives will be watching how Anthropic fares on the public markets, as they weigh their own investments in AI.

It has been revealed that luxury companies have been experimenting with AI across functions including customer service, merchandising, marketing and internal operations. The emergence of Anthropic as a publicly traded organization marks a new chapter for the providers developing the technology behind those applications.

According to recent reports, on the enterprise side, Anthropic has already found its way into the biggest luxury and beauty businesses. Earlier this year, LVMH group information officer Franck Le Moal remarked the group had strengthened its partnership with Anthropic and rolled out an internal platform built around Claude Code, designed to give its maisons secure access to AI tools. L’Oréal, meanwhile, uses Claude to develop specialized AI agents for workflows like conversational analytics across its business, while Kering has said it (occasionally) uses Claude Sonnet for software development, while mainly relying on Google Gemini and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

Industry observers note that A successful listing could reinforce confidence in the long-term prospects of AI, although it doesn’t necessarily mean the industry’s sky-high valuations are sustainable. For brands considering large-scale investments in AI tools, the more pertinent question is whether AI providers can establish durable, commercially viable businesses while continuing to improve their products.

Sources indicate that anthropic’s own brand positioning could also prove significant. Unlike some of its competitors, the manufacturer has made AI safety and responsible development central to its identity. In its IPO prospectus, Anthropic acknowledges that AI could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” if developed or deployed without adequate safeguards. The company also operates as a public benefit corporation, a structure requiring it to balance shareholders’ financial interests with its stated mission, as per its IPO prospectus, of “the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity”.

In a recent development, the IPO will put those commitments under greater scrutiny. Anthropic’s governance arrangements are designed in part to protect its mission, but going public also introduces fresh expectations around financial performance, sequential growth and shareholder returns. How the organization balances those pressures could influence its reputation among corporate customers.

Recent findings suggest that this AI safety positioning may resonate with luxury brands, whose value is underpinned by intellectual property, customer privacy and reputational control. But does Anthropic’s safety-focused identity offer a meaningful competitive advantage over rivals such as OpenAI and Google?

It has been revealed that not necessarily, according to creative agencies working with some of the world’s biggest brands. “We don’t hand clients one model,” says Gian-Carlo Lacanilao, director of creative innovation and AI at creative agency Made Thought, who explains that the agency often starts with Claude, then hand picks other AI models for different parts of a brief depending on which will do the job best.

Like Made Thought, Stephan Pretorius, chief technology officer at advertising group WPP, claims WPP takes a “model-agnostic” approach, selecting AI tools from the different hyperscalers — from Google to Amazon to OpenAI — according to the task, their performance and cost.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, the listing could have implications for luxury’s customer base. At the valuation targeted ahead of the IPO, Anthropic’s founders, employees and early investors stand to hold substantial stakes in one of the world’s most valuable technology companies.

It has been revealed that the flotation could contribute to a new wave of wealth creation in the US technology sector, particularly in Silicon Valley, at a time when luxury brands are seeking to strengthen relationships with high-spending clients with a focus on the US. Until now, much of that wealth has existed on paper, but now that the biggest companies in AI are hitting the public markets, analysts are poised for an influx of newly minted tech millionaires.

“The AI investment boom, accompanied by other factors, has been a major driver of global wealth creation in the last couple of years, and we expect tech’s share of the ultra-wealthy population to grow substantially over the next decade,” says Moira Boyle, global head of luxury, at wealth intelligence platform Altrata. “IPOs, acquisitions and secondary market sales are turning points, because they convert wealth on paper into wealth that can actually be spent.”.

Altrata tracks how the newly wealthy allocate their money, from investments through to discretionary spend. Boyle expects luxury goods to be a firm part of the picture — and says the “smartest” luxury houses are already adjusting to the changing face of the high-net-worth individual. She cites Hermès, for example, as a brand that’s been opening boutiques beyond the classic fashion capitals to meet new luxury clients (many of whom will, in this case, be Silicon Valley-based) where they actually live. “This cohort will shop differently. The average ultra-wealthy individual today is 67, and this new generation is decades younger, at a very different stage of life, with different passions and priorities,” she says. “Every brand now has an unprecedented opportunity to build relationships with these clients before their tastes and loyalties are set.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Green bean casserole belongs on every Thanksgiving spread. If you're scrambling to figure out how to perfect the classic side dish, look no further. I ditched the cream of mushroom soup for a homemade cream sauce and fresh sautéed mushrooms, but don’t worry—this dish is still super-simple to make. You only need 8 ingredients and a little over an hour to make it. Keep reading on for my top tips to make this classic side dish the best it can be:.

What People Are Saying:"Once you have this, you'll never be able to go back to the Campbell's gray sodium laden sludge & soggy canned green beans recipe! This is amazing! Your whole family will change their minds about green bean casserole." - CyanCarrot.

"This is the best green bean casserole I've ever made! It was easy enough that I could read it through twice, and then just make the dish without having to refer to the text of the recipe! It turned out great, my family ate it up! Without using a can of condensed soup, I could control the amount of salt...this made from scratch sauce tastes more mushroomy than a can of condensed soup!" - GreenBike.

The very first step is blanching the green beans. This may seem a little fussy, but it's the best way to start cooking the beans to preserve their crispy texture and bright green color as they continue to bake in the oven. It's easy, but just requires a little setup. Cook the beans in salted water for a few minutes, then immediately transfer to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking process. That's it!

On to the aromatics! This is what takes this casserole truly over the top. Cook sliced onions in butter until just starting to soften, anywhere from 7 to 10 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that add the mushrooms and let everyone get to know each other. Make it even better by adding some garlic; in my opinion, the more, the merrier. Your kitchen will smell amazing. Pour the aromatics into the bowl with the blanched beans.

Industry observers note that time for the sauce. No need to wipe out the pot, just melt a stick of butter, then toast the flour.

Slowly pour in the milk and whisk, letting the sauce come to a simmer, until nicely thickened. Be sure to taste for salt and pepper.

Recent findings suggest that add to bowl with beans, stir to combine, then transfer to a 13" x 9" baking dish. Spread in the dish, then bake until everything is bubbly, which should take just 30 minutes.

Time for the fried onions! Return to the oven and bake until the onions are just warmed through, about 5 minutes more.

The full list of ingredients and directions can be found in the recipe below.

Save some time (and oven space) on the busy holiday by making this Thanksgiving side ahead of time. Simply assemble the casserole (without the fried onions), cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for up to 4 days or until you're ready to bake!

It has been revealed that some tips: Make sure to let it cool to room temperature before baking, or add a couple of minutes to your timer to adjust to the colder temperature. Whatever you do, DON'T forget to add the fried onions until after the first round of baking. If they're added before refrigerating, they'll get soggy instead of having that signature crispy crunch.

Store any leftovers in an airtight container (or cover your casserole dish with storage wrap) before refrigerating. This side will last up to 4 days refrigerated (look through our Thanksgiving leftovers ideas for some creative inspo for what to do with them), and leftovers can be reheated in the microwave or oven.

Grand Theft Auto VI Review: Better Than The Hype

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are moments in GTA 6 that’ll have you levitating off your sofa.
  • Fronting the first franchise entry in more than 13 years are Jason and Lucia.
  • It has been revealed that this isn’t some kind of ChatGPT fantasy to indulge in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are moments in GTA 6 that’ll have you levitating off your sofa. Unprecedented in its scope and production, it was created by a team of almost 5,000 developers over nearly 10 years. Its budget is rumored to rival the construction of Dubai’s Burj Khalifa skyscraper; its first trailer set records with 93 million views in a day. Every social media brand account, from the White House to BMW, has jumped on the hype, while economists predict a national sick day as millions play hooky to game. When you do, you see the time, talent and flair on the screen. But, at its heart, Grand Theft Auto VI follows in series tradition: an epic American crime story, set in a stunning parody of the US that riffs on film, music, politics, style and satire.

Fronting the first franchise entry in more than 13 years are Jason and Lucia. Developer Rockstar attempted a multi-character arc in Grand Theft Auto V, but those three leads learned to loathe one another. Instead, VI tackles love, a game design challenge most developers have sworn off with good reason. Not a parent/child relationship like The Last of Us or God of War, but a mature, romantic, adult one. You can call or text each other at pretty much any point—to do missions together, commit robberies, explore, meditate, work out, fly, or just to coexist under the Vice City sunshine.

It has been revealed that this isn’t some kind of ChatGPT fantasy to indulge in. Neither Jason or Lucia exists at your beck and call as some kind of hyper-realistic plaything. You have a role in their relationship, both in the way they speak to each other and where the story takes them. You can cruise down the Vice City waterfront together in your souped-up ’70s muscle wagon with one of you driving, the other scrolling through your Snapmatic feed (the in-game social media channel), before grabbing a drink and carving up the sidewalk with an assault rifle five minutes later. You just don’t get these detours in Call of Duty.

More than a car: in GTA VI, your vehicle is a mobile base of operations to stash your guns, fits, money, and drugs.

Sources indicate that it’s a different pace from previous Grand Theft Autos too. Rockstar changed its dynamics with 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2—a more thoughtful take on the outlaw tale that added friction to the action and a conscience to the narrative. For a developer that once experienced the spotlight of US Congress during 2005’s infamous “Hot Coffee" controversy (when a sexually explicit mini-game meant as an inside joke between developers was figured out by savvy owners), this kind of nuance was revelatory. With VI, Rockstar takes Red Dead 2’s ethos and applies it to a modern city with 1,000 x the population. The result is staggering, but still an absolute blast to play. That is to say, the greatest hits of GTA—driving cars, shooting guns, and stealing money, drugs and more (all to spend on a better Beretta, G-Wagon replica, and impeccably modeled Air Jordan dupes)—but with added depth to how you play. Weapon slots are finite; you can no longer run amok with an entire arsenal stashed in your jacket pocket. Money is vulnerable; get killed or caught with cash in your possession, and you’ll lose it. And if you jack a car that’s fitted with a tracker, the police will find you swiftly.

Should you get into a bust-up with the law after a jewelry store smash-and-grab gone wrong, the game’s action is frenetic. Roads are much narrower, traffic is denser, and you can’t see police on your minimap. That $40,000 in cash sitting on the back seat had better be worth the hassle. As such, the game supports your decision to play chaotically, but truly immerses you in playing methodically. Jason and Lucia each have a “criminal profile”—be unnecessarily violent and you’ll get a “psycho” rating—that adds replayability and roleplay. Still, I had the most fun when planning missions: using a silenced pistol, shooting to maim not kill, and wiping security footage to leave no trace. It’s the closest GTA has honed in on the art of crime. The feds will surround the store you’re robbing. “Come out right now with your hands above your head!” Do things right, and you’ll have prepped your partner with a getaway car out back. You’ll leave the scene anonymously as backup blares past you on the other side of the road.

Every club, pub and dingy dive bar in GTA 6’s Leonida has a distinct vibe—from the music to the decor to the sweaty Floridians inside.

The game kicks off with an electrifying setup accompanied by an original song from composers Justice. It perfectly sets the tone: VI has the ’80s flamboyance of Vice City made new and fresh. It takes its opening hours steadily, sending you on odd jobs to make a little money here and there. Gradually—then suddenly—you’re thrust into the most high-octane campaign in Grand Theft Auto history. Tense hospital escapes, daring bank heists, cross-country chases, and more. Its set pieces are balls-to-the-wall bravado, rivaling what you’d see in Nolan’s The Odyssey or Villeneuve’s Dune, upping in intensity through its chapters. Tonally, it’s the most “of the now” Grand Theft Auto game yet, as your two in-love criminals race to find a better life in an unfair world. No previous GTA has given you a savings account—it’s like playing the millennial curse. The only dings are some pacing in the game’s second chapter as the game wrestles with its story while still introducing mechanics. Think of it as VI’s version of RDR2’s Guarma, albeit with bargain bin stores and grimy strip malls instead of exotic Caribbean fauna.

It has been revealed that and then to Leonida, with which Rockstar has created the most technically and artistically impressive game world ever made. The pre-release trailers promised beaches bustling with vacationers and nightclubs packed with dancers. That is the reality. From sea to sand to sky, the world is alive. Vice City alone could be an entire game in its own right, complete with distinct districts, an explorable international airport, and more. Yet, Rockstar spoils us with a massive expanse of varied towns, high-class beach resorts, lush green national parks, murky swamplands and sun-kissed island keys. All packed with people that range from useful, to funny, to completely unsavory (shout-out to the old woman who took one look at my Jason and said “I’mma take my teeth out and suck the skin off that dick”). The density and fidelity of it all often stretches the limits of even Sony’s PlayStation 5 Pro. Frame rate dips don’t spoil gameplay, but the slowdown is noticeable when you’ve punted a couple of grenades into passing cars to set off multiple explosions at once.

NPCs don’t just feel like backdrop mannequins anymore, but real people with an incredible range of faces, body types and outfits.

Sources indicate that every frame a photograph. Stop anywhere in GTA 6, and you’ll likely find something enticing to see, hear or interact with.

It has been revealed that as with Red Dead Redemption 2, the most impressive of the game’s many achievements is how everything seems to live on without you. All it took to make this world was Rockstar founding an entire studio to work solely on Leonida’s population. I’ve seen a woman throw herself out of a cop car window as I scooted along Ocean Beach, and car thieves burst through the glass windows of a car dealership while the alarms howl. I saw a furry taken down by armed police, staged perfectly with a helicopter spotlight. During one 3 a.m. wander through the rough neighborhood of Crosstown, a man approached me to warn me of the local gang and tells me they have a nearby base. I accidentally tapped the button that brings up your in-game phone. “Ohhhh! You don’t just believe what I say” the man states, responding to my actions. “You do your own research!” In more than 70 hours of play, I have seen only one moment of repetition.

Recent findings suggest that there is so much more besides. A cast of interesting, funny and believable characters; off-the-beaten-path secrets that can lead to side quests both major and small; perhaps the best radio track list of any GTA spanning from Travis Scott to Lana Del Rey; podcast episodes; golf to play; gators to hunt; dozens of supercars to steal and customize; weapons that feel punchy and satisfying; multiple racing series; a litany of actually interesting shops and bars and clubs to explore and buy things in. I’ve seen brilliant horror vignettes, startling science fiction, and laugh-out-loud comedy just by exploring. Rockstar has created a world that rewards you for spending time in it. Expect to spend 100 hours if you want to see everything.

According to recent reports, as you’ll likely have seen and heard—in everything from Miami Heat takeovers, to Netflix releases, to Selfridges pop-ups—that this is the most-wanted entertainment property in the world. In a way, all it had to be was Grand Theft Auto V: The Second. But, on the largest and most scrutinized stage imaginable, Rockstar takes creative risks with its story, protagonists, and mechanics, and makes big leaps in what games can be. It’s unlikely other developers will catch up soon. In 2002, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City reshaped and refashioned pop culture to give us a playable version of a place and a time we already knew. A quarter of a century later, VI indicates Rockstar at the peak of entertainment in its very own right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Recent findings suggest that whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a big pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

#42937. The Hidden Cost of a Hit Product
